title: 448. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Comparing Sine and Cosine Phase
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Express the sine function as a horizontal shift of the cosine function.
questions.question: Which identity expresses the sine as a shifted cosine for every real \(x\)?
questions.explanation: By the difference formula, \(\cos\left(x-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\cos x\cos\frac{\pi}{2}+\sin x\sin\frac{\pi}{2}=\sin x\). So the sine graph is the cosine graph shifted \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) to the right. The other expression equals \(-\sin x\).
questions.hint: Test both candidates at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\), where \(\sin x=1\).

questions.learningObjective: Express the cosine function as a horizontal shift of the sine function.
questions.question: Which identity expresses the cosine as a shifted sine for every real \(x\)?
questions.explanation: By the sum formula, \(\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\sin x\cos\frac{\pi}{2}+\cos x\sin\frac{\pi}{2}=\cos x\). So the cosine graph is the sine graph shifted \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) to the left. The other expression equals \(-\cos x\).
questions.hint: Test both candidates at \(x=0\), where \(\cos x=1\).

questions.concept: Direction of the shift from sine to cosine
questions.learningObjective: Describe the shift that maps the sine graph onto the cosine graph.
questions.question: Which horizontal shift maps the graph of \(y=\sin x\) onto the graph of \(y=\cos x\)?

options.label: A
options.text: A shift of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) units to the left

options.label: B
options.text: A shift of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) units to the right

questions.explanation: Shifting \(y=\sin x\) left by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) gives \(y=\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\cos x\). The maximum of the sine at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\) moves to \(x=0\), where the cosine has its maximum. A shift to the right gives \(y=\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=-\cos x\).
questions.hint: Compare where the two graphs reach their first maximum.

questions.concept: Fraction of a period between cosine and sine
questions.learningObjective: Express the phase difference between cosine and sine as a fraction of a period.
questions.question: The graphs of \(y=\cos x\) and \(y=\sin x\) have the same shape. By what fraction of a period does the cosine reach its maximum before the sine does?
questions.explanation: The cosine has a maximum at \(x=0\), and the sine has its next maximum at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\). The difference \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) is one quarter of the period \(2\pi\). A difference of half a period, \(\pi\), would turn a maximum into a minimum.
questions.hint: Find the first maximum of each function for \(x\ge 0\) and divide the difference by the period.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the effect of a half-period shift on the sine function.
questions.question: Which function is equal to \(y=\sin(x+\pi)\) for every real \(x\)?
questions.explanation: By the sum formula, \(\sin(x+\pi)=\sin x\cos\pi+\cos x\sin\pi=-\sin x\). A shift by half a period puts the graph exactly out of phase with the original, so every value changes sign. A shift by a quarter period, not a half period, turns the sine into the cosine.
questions.hint: Expand with the sine sum formula using \(\cos\pi=-1\) and \(\sin\pi=0\).

questions.learningObjective: Recognise a shifted cosine as a familiar function.
questions.question: Which function is equal to \(y=\cos\left(x-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) for every real \(x\)?
questions.explanation: By the difference formula, \(\cos\left(x-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\cos x\cdot 0+\sin x\cdot 1=\sin x\). Check at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\): \(\cos 0=1=\sin\frac{\pi}{2}\). The function \(-\sin x\) equals \(\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\).

questions.concept: Phase relation with a doubled argument
questions.learningObjective: Find the horizontal shift relating a sine and a cosine with the same coefficient of the variable.
questions.question: By how much must the graph of \(y=\sin 2x\) be shifted to the left to obtain the graph of \(y=\cos 2x\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(\cos 2x=\sin\left(2x+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\sin\left(2\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)\), the required shift is \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) to the left. This is a quarter of the period \(\pi\). Using \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) forgets to divide the phase by the coefficient \(2\).
questions.hint: Write \(\cos 2x\) as a sine and factor the coefficient of \(x\) out of the argument.

questions.learningObjective: Find where the sine and cosine graphs meet on one period.
questions.question: For \(0\le x<2\pi\), at which values of \(x\) do the graphs of \(y=\sin x\) and \(y=\cos x\) intersect?
questions.explanation: The graphs meet when \(\sin x=\cos x\), that is, \(\tan x=1\), which gives \(x=\frac{\pi}{4}\) and \(x=\frac{5\pi}{4}\). At \(x=\frac{3\pi}{4}\) the sine is \(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\) but the cosine is \(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\), so the graphs do not meet there.
questions.hint: Divide \(\sin x=\cos x\) by \(\cos x\) to obtain an equation in \(\tan x\).

questions.concept: A reflected cosine as a shifted sine
questions.learningObjective: Express a reflected cosine as a horizontal shift of the sine.
questions.question: Which function is equal to \(y=-\cos x\) for every real \(x\)?
questions.explanation: By the difference formula, \(\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\sin x\cos\frac{\pi}{2}-\cos x\sin\frac{\pi}{2}=-\cos x\). So \(-\cos x\) is the sine shifted \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) to the right. The expression \(\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) equals \(+\cos x\).
questions.hint: Expand both candidates with the sine sum and difference formulas, or test \(x=0\).

questions.concept: Rewriting a shifted sine as a cosine
questions.learningObjective: Convert a shifted sine into an equivalent shifted cosine.
questions.question: Which function is equal to \(y=\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\) for every real \(x\)?
questions.explanation: Use \(\sin u=\cos\left(u-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) with \(u=x-\frac{\pi}{6}\): \(\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\cos\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\cos\left(x-\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\). The expression \(\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\) is \(\cos\left(u+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=-\sin u\), which has the opposite sign.
questions.hint: Replace the sine by a cosine whose argument is smaller by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\), then combine the constants.
